## Fifth refactoring complete: `libs/core/.../IOUtils.java`

The two collecting `close(...)` overloads — `close(Exception ex, Closeable... objects)` and `close(Iterable<? extends Closeable> objects)` — had an identical try/catch-and-collect loop body, differing only in the initial `firstException` value and whether they iterate a varargs array or an `Iterable`.

I extracted the per-element step into a private `closeAndCollect(firstException, object)` helper: it closes one `Closeable` and folds any failure into the running first-exception (returning it as-is when there was no prior exception, else adding it as suppressed). Each loop is now a one-liner. This rounds out the close-family, which already had `addOrSuppress` and `throwRuntimeOrIOException` factored out.

### Why not fully merge the two methods
A varargs `Closeable[]` is not an `Iterable`, so unifying the loops would require wrapping the array (e.g. `Arrays.asList`) — an allocation on a cleanup path that runs constantly. This Lucene-derived code deliberately keeps the array loop allocation-free, so I kept both loops and shared only the allocation-free per-element body. I documented this reasoning in the helper's Javadoc.

### Behavior-preservation
Bit-identical, including suppressed-exception ordering: when `close(object)` succeeds, `closeAndCollect` returns the same `firstException`; when it throws, it returns `addOrSuppress(firstException, e)` — exactly the original control flow. The helper is `private static`, so the JVM inlines it; no allocation, no extra object.

### Verification
- `IOUtils` compiled cleanly (exit 0) against a minimal `Nullable` stub (the full `libs/core` package can't compile standalone because sibling files `XmlUtils`/`Nullable` need `org.elasticsearch.logging` and `javax.annotation`, which are unrelated to this change).
- Same standing caveat: the Gradle test suite (`:libs:core:test`, incl. `IOUtilsTests`) couldn't run here — worth a CI run before merge.

Five compile-verified deduplication refactors now: `DissectKey`, `DissectParser`, `WellKnownBinary`, `WellKnownText`, `IOUtils`. Happy to continue.
